summary: Preserved candidate PR 1965's complete idle RadixCache reset and added safe teardown/rebootstrap for a live disaggregated-prefill chunk. Retract now aborts the live KV sender, releases its metadata slot, retracts its KV, resets all cache/pool namespaces, and requeues it through a fresh prefill bootstrap.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing before: a separately inserted four-token prefix remained matchable 4/4; the unfinished PREFILL chunk remained retained and allocator clear count was zero.
36 tests passed and 2 subtests passed, covering idle and active retract, hierarchical reset semantics, live PREFILL sender teardown/requeue, and radix lock references.

tests.command: Corrected inline simulated-RadixCache live PREFILL probe
tests.what_was_measured: Passing after: prefix match changed from 4/4 before pause to 0/4 after pause; chunk was not retained, sender abort ran once, allocator clear ran once, and requeue ran once.
25 disaggregated-prefill abort, bootstrap, and chunked-abort race tests passed.

tests.command: Torch CUDA tensor square on the assigned device
tests.what_was_measured: One AMD Instinct MI355X was visible and produced [1.0, 4.0] from [1.0, 2.0] squared.

gpu_execution.evidence: A basic Torch device operation executed on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X. The issue-specific scheduler/RadixCache regression itself is deterministic CPU simulation.

remaining_limitations: No Qwen model weights were available, so the reported old/new-weight logprob and text divergence were not reproduced.

No multi-node disaggregated deployment was available; transport abort and fresh bootstrap behavior were validated through existing scheduler interfaces and deterministic unit fixtures, not live RDMA transfer.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
